We need to compute total time for light traveling Earth -> first exoplanet (distance 4.22 ly), then from first exoplanet to second exoplanet (distance 6.1 ly), then from second exoplanet back to Earth (distance 5.88 ly). Sum distances: 4.22 + 6.1 + 5.88 = 16.2 ly. Then convert to seconds: 1 ly = distance light travels in one year. Light travels 1 ly in one year. So 16.2 ly = 16.2 years. But we can also compute using speed of light: 1 ly = c * 1 year. So time = distance / speed. But easier: 16.2 years. Convert to seconds: 1 year ~ 365.25 days * 24h * 3600s = 31557600 s. Multiply by 16.2: 31557600 * 16.2 = 511,? Let's compute: 31,557,600 * 16 = 504,921,600. Add 0.2 * 31,557,600 = 6,311,520. Sum = 511,233,120 seconds. So about 5.112e8 seconds.
